title: Microsoft Teams Rooms: IntelliFrame people labels name in-room participants
summary: Hold: the briefing calls the arrival default unknown even though Microsoft's notice says eligible rooms receive the feature automatically. The recognition command omits a documented prerequisite, the enrollment command does not disable every enrollment method, and the claim that no label cap is documented conflicts with the published participant limit.

Replace the claims that the arrival default is unstated with: "Microsoft's notice says the labels are enabled automatically when prerequisites are met, with no action required to enable the feature. claims.claim: People must be included in the meeting invitation to be identified.

claims.claim: No autonomous actions on behalf of users are documented for the people-label feature.

claims.claim: Learn documents missing name labels in Active speaker view rather than IntelliFrame view.

claims.quote: For people Identification, the Outlook invite supports a total of 64 users, which includes both users attending online and up to 12 concurrent users in the room for Name labels.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost

claims.claim: The cited Learn prerequisites and supplied notice name no other required license for labels.
claims.quote: Searched: "IntelliFrame" "people labels" "price" meter cap. Opened all three cited Learn pages and read MC1419798; their label/recognition prerequisites name Teams Rooms Pro and no additional labels license.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate label meter or price is documented on the reviewed feature pages.
claims.quote: Searched: "IntelliFrame" "people labels" "price" meter cap. Opened multistream-intelliframe, teams-rooms-people-recognition and voice-and-face-recognition; read MC1419798. No separate label price or billing meter was stated.

claims.quote: For people Identification, the Outlook invite supports a total of 64 users, which includes both users attending online and up to 12 concurrent users in the room for Name labels.

claims.claim: The cited feature pages do not publish the Teams Rooms Pro price.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams Rooms Pro" "price" "$40". Opened the three cited feature pages; none quotes a Teams Rooms Pro price. This confirms only the page-scoped absence, not that Microsoft has never published Pro pricing elsewhere.

claims.claim: The multi-stream page lists Jabra Panacast 50, Lenovo ThnkSmart Bar 180, Yealink SmartVision 40, Yealink SmartVision 60 and Yealink MVC S90 Bundle as supported devices.
claims.quote: These Microsoft Teams Rooms devices support Multi-Stream IntelliFrame and people recognition. ... Jabra Panacast 50; Lenovo ThnkSmart Bar 180; Yealink SmartVision 40; Yealink SmartVision 60; Yealink MVC S90 Bundle

claims.claim: Learn says additional cameras may become certified over time.
claims.quote: Additional cameras may become certified over time.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <PolicyName> -roomPeopleNameUserOverride On is the complete documented meeting-policy enablement call for people recognition.
claims.quote: Enabling people recognition requires the tenant CsTeamsMeetingPolicy roomPeopleNameUserOverride to be "On" and roomAttributeUserOverride to be Attribute for allowing individual voice and face profiles to be used for recognition in meetings.
claims.fix: Replace controls[0].api.call and its rendered call with "Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <PolicyName> -roomAttributeUserOverride Attribute -roomPeopleNameUserOverride On". That full call is printed on the existing controls[0].api.docs page, https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/rooms/teams-rooms-people-recognition. Qualify the meeting-policy enablement advice with "with roomAttributeUserOverride set to Attribute".

claims.claim: No Teams admin center path is documented for setting roomPeopleNameUserOverride.
claims.quote: Searched: "roomPeopleNameUserOverride" "admin center". Opened teams-rooms-people-recognition and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; results document PowerShell for this policy, not a Teams admin center path.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: roomPeopleNameUserOverride controls video identification with On and Off values.
claims.quote: roomPeopleNameUserOverride | Control the video-based user identification in meeting rooms. | Off - The room won't send video for identification. On - Room users captured by supported cameras will be identified.

claims.claim: The meeting-policy recognition control has user scope.
claims.quote: The Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy cmdlet allows administrators to update existing meeting policies that can be assigned to particular users to control Teams features related to meetings.

claims.claim: Recognition device settings are configured in Teams Pro Management Portal through Rooms > Settings > Recognition > Configure with device settings > Apply > Submit.
claims.quote: Select Rooms. Select Settings followed by the Recognition tab. Enable Configure with device settings. Modify to the desired configuration. Select Apply. Choose when to apply the settings change and select Submit.

claims.claim: No API is documented for the Pro Management Portal device-recognition settings.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams Rooms" "Recognition" "API" "device"; Pro Management Portal recognition PowerShell API. Opened people-recognition, pro-portal-settings and xml-config-file; no recognition-device-setting API was found.

claims.claim: Recognition can also be configured locally on the Teams Room console.
claims.quote: On the Teams Room console, go to Settings > Recognition. Select Configure with device settings (Recommended). Turn on Voice recognition and/or Face recognition as applicable.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy -Identity Global -EnrollVoice Disabled -EnrollFace Disabled controls whether users can enroll voice and face profiles across enrollment methods.
claims.quote: This setting can also be individually set to Enabled or Disabled and operates independently of EnrollVoice. ... To turn off voice enrollment completely, make sure to set both parameters to Disable.
claims.fix: Narrow controls[2].governs and the rendered row heading to "Whether users may actively enrol voice and face profiles". Replace the note's claim that the call is the cited page's Global example with "Disables active voice and face enrolment for the Global policy; express voice enrolment is controlled separately by PassiveVoiceEnrollment." The cited enrollment article explicitly distinguishes these methods. Keep the existing valid call for this narrower purpose.

claims.claim: No admin UI is documented for configuring CsTeamsAIPolicy enrollment permissions.
claims.quote: Searched: "CsTeamsAIPolicy" "admin center" "enrollment". Opened voice-and-face-recognition; read the copilot-admin-mtr search excerpt: "There isn't a way to set this in Teams admin center. You must use PowerShell."

claims.claim: CsTeamsAIPolicy is accessible only through PowerShell.
claims.quote: You can access this policy only through Microsoft PowerShell.

claims.claim: New-CsTeamsAIPolicy creates a custom policy for specific users' enrollment permissions.
claims.quote: To disable active voice and face enrollment for specific users, Enterprise administrators can create and assign a custom meeting policy to the users: New-CsTeamsAIPolicy -Identity DisableEnrollment -EnrollVoice Disabled -EnrollFace Disabled

claims.claim: Grant-CsTeamsAIPolicy assigns the custom policy to specific users.
claims.quote: This cmdlet applies an instance of the Teams AI policy to users or groups in a tenant. ... Passes in the Identity of the policy instance in the PolicyName parameter and the user identifier in the Identity parameter

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Teams admin center can show end-user voice and face enrollment status.
claims.quote: Enterprise administrators can now use Teams admin center to view end-user voice and face enrollment status and manage enrolled data directly from the admin experience.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Administrators can delete end-user voice and face profiles in Teams admin center.

claims.claim: Administrators cannot export end-user enrollment data from Teams admin center.
claims.quote: Enterprise administrators can't export end-user voice or face enrollment data from the Teams admin center. Export of enrollment data remains under the end user's control and within the user experience.

claims.claim: The cited enrollment article gives no Teams admin center navigation path for reviewing status or deleting profiles.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams voice face enrollment Teams admin center enrollment status delete profiles path. Opened voice-and-face-recognition in full; its Manage enrollment data in Teams admin center section states the capabilities but gives no navigation steps.

claims.claim: Individual users can opt out by removing their profile in Teams > Settings > Recognition.
claims.quote: Individual users can opt out anytime by removing their profile in Teams > Settings > Recognition.

claims.claim: Learn does not state precedence between the recognition device settings and meeting-policy method when both are set.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams Rooms" "recognition" "device settings" "precedence". Opened people-recognition, pro-portal-settings and xml-config-file; the recognition instructions describe alternative methods without a precedence rule.

claims.claim: The Teams Rooms release notes describe recognition device settings as replacing PowerShell configuration.
claims.quote: These settings replace PowerShell-based configuration with a more intuitive UI, offering clearer visibility into recognition status across rooms.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/rooms/rooms-release-note to sources for the release-note statement.

claims.claim: Users start enrollment in Teams > Settings > Recognition.
claims.quote: Enrollment starts in the Teams app: users go to Settings > Recognition

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist directs administrators to review and delete enrollment profiles, but the controls table has no row for that control.
claims.quote: After rollout: "Review enrolment status and remove profiles where needed in the Teams admin center". The table covers name-display policy, device recognition and enrollment permissions, not enrollment-profile review or deletion.
claims.fix: Remove the After rollout checklist bullet beginning "Review enrolment status and remove profiles where needed". The supported capability can remain in the Governance controls prose without adding an unverified table path.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice says labels create no new data and rely on existing People Recognition voice and face profiles.
claims.quote: This feature does not create new data; it relies on existing voice and face profiles from People Recognition enrollment, governed by the organization’s current configuration.

claims.claim: Device recognition settings and Teams meeting policies are separate configuration methods.
claims.quote: Recognition in Teams Rooms can be configured through either device-level settings or a Teams Meeting policy.

claims.where: licensing.notes; What's changing; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Learn lists Teams Rooms Pro as a prerequisite and says people recognition is exclusive to Pro-licensed Teams Rooms devices.
claims.quote: This feature is exclusive to Microsoft Teams Rooms devices with a Teams Rooms Pro license.
